issues.title: Computed association support threshold is silently overwritten by literal 5
issues.defect: V550J computes and uses a governed/dynamic association support threshold, then the same Python dict literal assigns `association_support_threshold` again with hard-coded value 5. Python silently keeps the later value.
issues.evidence: Duplicate-key hostile scan traced both assignments in the authoritative row constructor. The publication decision can be made under one threshold while emitted audit/provenance claims threshold 5.
issues.consequence: Audit output can misstate the statistical gate that actually authorized or blocked association evidence, defeating reproducibility and downstream review.
issues.required: Emit the actual effective governed threshold exactly once. Add duplicate-dict-key/static regression coverage to the touched module.
tests: Construct a case with effective threshold != 5 and verify emitted threshold equals the decision threshold.
No duplicate dict key for association_support_threshold.

issues.title: Governed association-lane publishability is discarded and recomputed by shadowed hard-coded policy
issues.defect: The installed association-lane registry supplies explicit lane publishability/classification authority, but the current path discards the registry's publishability field and later recomputes publishability through a duplicated/shadowed hard-coded `_association_lane_publishability` function.
issues.evidence: A constructed registry result marking a lane blocked can be relabeled according to hard-coded policy. The definitive ledger identifies the registry as CONDITIONAL_ASSOCIATION_CLASSIFIER authority.
issues.consequence: Governed policy can be overridden by code defaults; shadowed definitions make the override unstable and opaque.
issues.required: Treat registry publishability as authoritative when association mode is active. Remove the competing hard-coded semantic state machine; keep only an explicit legacy/fallback path if governance authorizes one, and fail closed when governed registry is required but missing.
tests: Registry says blocked -> emitted lane cannot become publishable.
No materially different shadowed publishability functions remain authoritative.

issues.title: Main rejects draft family authority while shipping a draft default registry
issues.defect: Current main correctly treats `draft` family registries as non-executable, but the default question-family registry it ships is itself status=draft. The August runtime donor instead treats draft as executable.
issues.evidence: Exhaustive reconciliation found main's stricter executable-status contract and the shipped registry label. This promotes WATCH-004 into a mandatory coherence problem for the integrated pipeline.
issues.consequence: A direct default V550J invocation either fails on its shipped registry or reconciliation can accidentally reintroduce the runtime's weaker 'draft is executable' behavior.
issues.required: Preserve main's stricter governance semantics. Resolve the default invocation coherently: supply/reissue an explicitly executable governed registry for the intended scope, or make joint authority optional/applicability-scoped rather than silently executing draft authority.
tests: Draft registry is never silently executable.
A default/declared V550J mode either has executable governed family authority or reports typed not-applicable/authority-missing state.
